prop:native-gravity-firstjet.title: Literal gravitational consistency from strong first jets
prop:native-gravity-firstjet.note: Proved in the unit-torus rendering of the paper's periodic comparison box (grid (Z/N)^4, mesh h = 1/N; the side-2pi box is its dilation, as for prop:native-Higgs-compactness), for the ACTUAL literal gravitational row S_{g,h}^loc(y) = h^4 sum_x L_{g,h}(y)(x) of eq:native-densities (NativeDensity.gravityDensity: Cartan plaquette logarithm of L_mu = exp(h Omega_mu(e, delta^+ e))) on records y of the native local action, varied along the nodal symmetric lift eq:metric-lift (liftM, liftM_apply: edot^a_mu = -1/2 e^a_alpha g_{mu beta} k^{alpha beta}) of the sampled test k(x/N) (gravVariation = deriv_t S_{g,h}(y + t I_h k) at 0). Hypotheses exactly as in the paper: coframes in one compact oriented nondegenerate chart K_e subset {det > 0}; the common logarithm-chart condition eq:native-gravity-log-margin h|omega_{mu,h}| <= c_* with an explicit c_* <= 1/64 in the entrywise sup norm (the paper's 'fixed c_* on which the four-exponential plaquette product and its logarithm are analytic': c_* <= 1/64 implies ||P - 1|| < 1, norm_plaqDev_lt_of_margin / cartan_log_lt); R^0 e_h -> e and R^0 D^+_mu e_h -> p_mu strongly in L^2 (eq:native-coframe-firstjet; p_mu = d_mu e entrywise by firstJet_eq_weakDeriv). Conclusion (native_gravity_firstjet): for every eps > 0, eventually |D S_{g,h}^loc(e_h)[I_h k] - D S_{g,theta}(e)[k]| <= eps ||k||_{C^2} for ALL tests k simultaneously, i.e. the sup over the C^2 unit ball tends to 0, which gives eq:native-gravity-firstvariation for every r >= 2 (||k||_{C^2} <= ||k||_{C^r}; tests rendered as C2Test: continuous M4-valued fields on T^4 with continuous coordinate partials up to order 2, norm sup|k| + sum sup|d k| + sum sup|dd k|). The continuum D S_{g,theta}(e)[k] (contGravVariation) is the first variation of the first-order Palatini action int L^(1)(e, de), L^(1) = palatiniFirstOrder, identified in palatiniFirstOrder_eq as sum pal(e)[omega_mu, omega_nu] - sum (D_e C^{mu nu}[p_mu]) omega_nu - (Lambda/kappa) v(e) with omega = Omega(e, p) (the representative -dB wedge omega + B wedge omega wedge omega - (Lambda/kappa)v of eq:palatini-first-order, app:palatini), along (edot, d edot) = (lift(e,k), lift(e, dk) + D_e lift(e,k)[de]) (hasDerivAt_liftM); contGravVariation_eq_deriv / hasDerivAt_palatiniAction prove it is the derivative in the lift of the action (differentiation under the integral, dominated by C(1+|p|)^2). Proof exactly along the paper's route: first-jet normal form (sum_gravityDensity_eq from gravityDensity_eq_curl + sum_curl_eq: curl moved by discrete summation by parts onto the Palatini coefficient, exact quadratic remainder Rem = Q_h(W)); the coframe jet density gravCurv is exactly homogeneous of degree two under (h, q) -> (hK, q/K) (gravCurv_scale; remPlaquette_smul, dqPal_smul) and smooth on the compact normalised chart (contDiffAt_gravCurv, isCompact_gravChart); the generic theorem HomogeneousJetVariation.lpTendsto_homogeneous_variation (new, no renewal notions) turns the degree-two growth into bounded coefficients converging in measure times L^1-convergent products of the strongly convergent first differences (lem:products, LpProductContinuity.LpTendsto.coeff), giving strong L^1 convergence of the variation covectors (lpTendsto_gridCov); grid sums are integrals of raw reconstructions (integral_pc) and the sampled test jets converge uniformly at rate 3/N ||k||_{C^2} (norm_pc_testJet_sub_le), which gives the uniform C^2-dual estimate. Second clause (native_gravity_firstjet_reconstructed): for any continuum reconstructions f_h in the same compact chart with first jets g_h, f_h -> e and g_h -> de strongly in L^2 (strong H^1), the consistency error relative to the reconstructed coframes tends to 0 uniformly on the C^2 unit ball (continuum continuity lpTendsto_limitCov = gravity sector of prop:reduced-continuity in this rendering). No growing band, C^5 or curvature-discrepancy hypothesis is used. Disclosed renderings: unit torus; real 4x4 coframe matrices in one trivialised chart; tests periodic C^2 fields (the paper's compactly supported smooth tests in the box are such fields); the inverse-metric tests are not required to be symmetric (the theorem holds for all real 4x4 test fields, in particular the symmetric ones). Non-vacuity: example with the flat records (identity coframe, chart {1}, c_* = 0). Standard axioms only.

thm:native-firstvariation-no-band.title: All-sector native consistency without a growing band
thm:native-firstvariation-no-band.note: Clause-level: ALL CLAUSES PROVED. Main assertions and Euler corollary under (N1)-(N5): unchanged from e33 (NativeAllSectorGraph.native_all_sector_closure, NativeBank.native_all_sector_closure_bank; pointers kept). FINAL PARAGRAPH (consistency relative to the complete unfiltered reconstructed fields), e36 follow-up: INSTANTIATED with the trigonometric interpolants (new file Continuum/NativeTrigReconstructedFields.lean). native_reconstructed_closure_trig (fixed bank) and native_reconstructed_closure_trig_bank (varying banks): the hypotheses are exactly (N1)-(N4)/(N5) of native_all_sector_closure(_bank) plus the two hypotheses of the final paragraph (the complete unfiltered reconstructed coframes I_h e_h stay in the same compact chart; ordinary connection first differences R0 D+_mu A_nu,h -> P_munu strongly in L2); the reconstructed fields are I_h z_h = recon (componentwise real parts of TorusTrigReconstruction.trigInterp in a basis) with classical first jets drecon = d_mu I_h (Fourier multiplier 2 pi i m_mu on the symbol coefficients), for gravity, YM, Higgs AND Dirac (spinor jets recJets = (d I_h Psi, d I_h Psibar)). Every comparison estimate eq:native-reconstruction-comparison used by the abstract theorem is PROVED for I_h, not assumed: L2 convergence from raw L2 convergence plus the discrete H1 bound (recon_tendsto_of_bounded, via eLpNorm_trigInterp_sub_pc_le_grad), jets d I_h u - R0 D+ u -> 0 strongly when R0 D+ u converges (tendsto_dTrigLp, symbol estimate norm_dTrigLp_le) and WEAKLY and boundedly when D+ u is only bounded (weak_dTrig_sub_pc: Fourier-coefficient convergence + trig-polynomial density; drecon_weak, drecon_bounded), L4 convergence of I_h A_h, I_h H_h (tendsto_eLpNorm_four_trig: critical Sobolev NativeCoulomb.eLpNorm_four_trigPoly_le + H1 subset L4 truncation), uniform L4 bounds of the reconstructed spinors (recon_eLpNorm_four_bounded), assembled for the spinors from SpinHyp + the positive spinor graph outputs in spinor_rec_data. Conclusions along one extraction: eq:native-all-sector-limit; F = P - P^T + [A,A] a.e.; sectorwise consistency errors at the trigonometric fields -> 0 (gravity at (I_h e_h, d I_h e_h), YM at (I_h e_h, I_h A_h, F(I_h A_h)), Higgs at (I_h e_h, I_h A_h, I_h H_h, d I_h H_h), Dirac-Yukawa at (I_h Psi_h, I_h Psibar_h) with jets recJets) and the total error. The ABSTRACT version (arbitrary reconstructions satisfying the comparison estimates) is kept as a lemma: NativeReconstructed.native_reconstructed_closure(_bank) (file NativeReconstructedConsistency.lean, with the sectorwise continuity theorems). Renderings: unit torus, trivialised bundles, Higgs fibre R^rH, kappa = id, I_h on the symmetric frequency box (-N/2, N/2]^4, vector fields componentwise in Module.finBasis. Non-vacuity: flat records (example after native_reconstructed_closure_trig_bank: trigInterp of a constant is the constant, recon_const, so the chart hypothesis holds) and the abstract example in NativeReconstructedConsistency.lean. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

thm:native-Wilson-compactness.title: Direct native Wilson compactness
thm:native-Wilson-compactness.note: Both assertions proved on the entire periodic box (grid conventions and 2π-dilation as in lem:native-discrete-KR, any d). Unitary internal representation: represented links ρ(U_μ(x)) are linear isometry equivalences of a finite-dimensional complex fibre F; openLink = eq:open-finite-link, wilsonShift = eq:finite-Wilson-shift; the Wilson screen eq:native-Wilson-compactness (Ω_h of eq:finite-Wilson-modulus summed over the whole box) is used for positive displacements 0 < m h <= ρ only, in the form 'for every ε there is ρ with eventually all these Wilson differences <= ε in L^2_h' (implied by the paper's hypothesis). Scalar assertion (no connection bound, any links/site gauge): |R^0 Y_h| totally bounded in L^2(𝕋^d;ℝ) (…_magnitude_totallyBounded_real; complex-valued form …_magnitude_totallyBounded) and |R^0 Y_h|^2 uniformly integrable (UnifIntegrable (R^0 Y_h) 2, i.e. sup_h ∫_E |R^0Y_h|^2 -> 0 as |E| -> 0), via the grid Kato inequality, native_discrete_KR and lem:compact-magnitude-ui (compactMagnitude_unifIntegrable, proved). Vector assertion: native_wilson_vector_totallyBounded_exp with links ρ(U_μ(x)) = exp(h dρ(A_μ(x))) (U_h = e^{hA_h}), dρ: 𝔤 ->L[ℝ] End(F) skew-adjoint-valued (F a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space), sup_h ||A_h||_{2,h} <= M_A; proof exactly as the paper: unitarity gives ||exp(hX)-1|| <= h||X|| (mean value, unitary exp(tX)), telescoping ||P_{μ,m}-I|| <= Σ_j h a(x+j e_μ), amplitude split giving eq:native-Wilson-ordinary-modulus ||T_mY-Y||_{2,h} <= Ω_h + R m h M_A + 2 q_h(R) (gridNorm_shift_sub_le_wilson), q_h(R) -> 0 uniformly from the uniform integrability (exists_tail_le, via UniformIntegrable.spec'), then native_discrete_KR. The general form native_wilson_vector_totallyBounded takes the link bound ||ρ(U_μ(x))v - v|| <= h a_μ(x)||v||, ||a_μ||_{2,h} <= M_A directly. Buffered-chart (local) version mentioned at the end of the paper's proof is not formalised (the theorem statement is the full-box one).

lem:native-discrete-Hodge.title: Exact periodic discrete Hodge identity
lem:native-discrete-Hodge.note: periodicHodge_identity: on any finite additive commutative group X (the periodic grid, e.g. (ZMod N)^4) with lattice steps e_mu, directions a finite linearly ordered type (Fin 4), values in a real inner product space (Lie algebra with invariant inner product), and every mesh h, sum_{mu,nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu||^2_{2,h} = ||d_h^+ A||^2_{2,h} + ||delta_h A||^2_{2,h}, with ||u||^2_{2,h} = h^{dim} sum_x |u(x)|^2, D^+ forward difference, delta_h A = -sum_mu D^-_mu A_mu (eq:native-discrete-divergence), ||d^+A||^2 = sum_{mu<nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu - D^+_nu A_mu||^2. Proof in position space (translation invariance of periodic sums) rather than Fourier. periodicHodge_H1_bound: for h >= 0, ||A||_{1,h} <= 1*(||d^+A|| + ||delta A|| + ||A||_{2,h}) with ||A||^2_{1,h} = sum_nu ||A_nu||^2 + sum_{mu,nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu||^2 (C = 1, uniform in h).

thm:native-discrete-Coulomb.title: Critical discrete Coulomb compactness
thm:native-discrete-Coulomb.note: Proved (NativeCoulomb.native_discrete_Coulomb), unit-torus rendering (grid (Z/N)^4, mesh h = 1/N, side 1; the paper's odd grids of side 2pi are the dilation, every N allowed). Disclosed renderings: connections take values in a finite-dimensional complete normed complex algebra A with ||1|| = 1 (e.g. M_n(C) with the operator norm, containing the compact gauge algebras; complex scalars only enter the Cauchy estimate of the plaquette remainder); the Lie-algebra norms are read in a real inner product space E through T : A ->L[R] E with ||X|| <= c||T X|| (Frobenius identification for u(n)); the smallness ||A_h||_{4,h} <= eps* is imposed componentwise (||T A_{h,mu}||_{4,h} <= eps* for every mu, weaker than the summed norm); eps* = 1/(69120(||T||+1)(c+1)^2) is explicit. Statement: there is eps* > 0 such that for every sequence of grids N_k -> oo and nodal connections with delta_h T A_k = 0 (codiffT = -sum_mu D^-_mu, the paper's eq:native-discrete-divergence), ||T A_{k,mu}||_{4,h} <= eps* and R_h^0 F_h(A_k) -> F strongly in L^2 (F_h = curvLog, the literal logarithmic plaquette), after extraction: R_h^0 A_k -> A strongly in L^4; R_h^0 D+_mu A_{k,nu} -> G_{mu nu} strongly in L^2 with G_{mu nu} = d_mu A_nu (Fourier side, every frequency); for every complex coordinate l of A, l A_nu in H^1 and the trigonometric reconstructions I_h^trig(l A_k) -> l A in H^1; F = F_A pointwise a.e. (F_{mu nu} = d_mu A_nu - d_nu A_mu + [A_mu, A_nu]); delta A = 0 (sum_mu d_mu A_mu = 0 a.e.). Proof as in the manuscript, all clauses formalized: (i) the Lipschitz half of eq:native-YM-envelope, ||N_h(A) - N_h(B)|| <= 5(|W(A)| + |W(B)|)|W(A-B)| pointwise and its L^2_h form (norm_nonlin_sub_le, gridNorm_nonlin_sub_le; from the new Cauchy-estimate Lipschitz bound for the cubic BCH remainder, PlaquetteLogDerivative.norm_bchRem_sub_le); (ii) the absorption inequality eq:native-Coulomb-explicit-absorption with explicit constants (coulomb_absorption: exact Hodge identity + uniform grid Sobolev + envelope), which with B = 0 is the a priori H^1 bound; (iii) discrete Rellich componentwise, L^1 convergence of the nonlinear term and the exact Fourier multipliers of the grid differences identify F = dA + A^A and delta A = 0 on the Fourier side; (iv) comparison fields = Fourier truncations P_R A of the limit (divergence free; P_R A -> A in L^2 and, by the new critical embedding H^1(T^4) c L^4 obtained from the discrete Sobolev inequality by sampling, tendsto_eLpNorm_four_trunc, in L^4; F_{P_R A} -> F), sampled on the grids with fixed-smooth-field consistency; absorption gives limsup_h ||D+A_h - dP_R A||_{L^2} <= c delta_R -> 0, hence the forward differences are Cauchy in L^2 (exists_tendsto_differences); (v) lem:native-reconstruction-identification gives the L^4 and trigonometric H^1 statements and prop:native-YM-identification (first assertion, native_YM_curvature_identification) gives F = F_A pointwise. The convention bridge between CoulombAprioriEstimate/PeriodicForwardDifferenceHodgeIdentityExact (general mesh h, side L = n h, E-valued) and the unit-torus files is NativeCoulombAbsorption (h = 1/N, L = 1, periodicHodgeNormSq = gridNorm^2, gridFwd = DpV, T-read values); the a priori estimate is reproved there in unit-torus notation (coulomb_apriori'). Non-vacuity: example at the end of NativeCoulombCompactness (zero connections in A = C). Standard axioms only.

lem:native-log-gauge-differential.title: Exact logarithmic site-gauge differential
lem:native-log-gauge-differential.note: Both identities proved on the periodic grid (Z/n)^iota (any finite iota, any mesh h != 0), with the gauge group in the units of an arbitrary complete normed real algebra A (nontrivial; for SU(3)xSU(2): pairs of complex matrices) and Lie-algebra fields A_mu(x), xi_x in A, ad_A u = Au - uA. New generic infrastructure (Algebra/MatrixExpDerivative.lean, absent from Mathlib, which differentiates exp only along commuting directions): Duhamel e^A - e^B = int_0^1 e^{sA}(A-B)e^{(1-s)B} ds; D exp(X)[Y] = int_0^1 e^{sX} Y e^{(1-s)X} ds; e^{s ad_X}Y = e^{sX}Y e^{-sX}; int_0^1 e^{sZ} ds = J(Z) = sum Z^k/(k+1)! (OperatorHalfCoth.dexpJ); hence the dexp formula D exp(X)[Y] = (J(ad_X)Y) e^X (fderiv_exp_eq, the paper's left-trivialized U'U^{-1} = h J(Z) A'); strict differentiability with invertible derivative when J(ad_X) is a unit (e.g. ||X|| <= 1/8); every local left inverse Log of exp near X (the logarithm chart) is strictly differentiable at e^X with derivative W -> J(ad_X)^{-1}(W e^{-X}) (hasStrictFDerivAt_log_of_eventually); d/dt Log(e^{t xi} e^X e^{-t eta})|_0 = J(ad_X)^{-1}(xi - e^{ad_X} eta). Gauge application (GaugeTheory/LogarithmicSiteGaugeDifferential.lean): gaugeCurve = A^{q(t)}_mu(x) = h^{-1} Log(e^{t xi_x} e^{hA_mu(x)} e^{-t xi_{x+e_mu}}). gauge_differential (eq:native-gauge-differential): if Log(e^Y) = Y near every h A_mu(x) (any fixed chart containing the scaled links; conjugation invariance not needed) and every J(h ad_{A_mu(x)}) is invertible, then A^{q(0)} = A and d/dt A^{q(t)}_mu(x)|_0 = -K(h ad_{A_mu}) D^+_mu xi(x) - [A_mu(x), m_mu xi(x)], K(Z) = (Z/2)coth(Z/2) = 1/2 J(Z)^{-1}(I + e^Z) (OperatorHalfCoth.halfCoth), via J^{-1}(I - e^Z) = -Z exactly as in the paper. gauge_energy_differential (eq:native-gauge-energy-differential): for any symmetric continuous bilinear form <.,.> on A with <A_mu(x), [A_mu(x), u]> = 0 (implied by ad-invariance + symmetry of the paper's positive invariant metric, e.g. Re tr(X^*Y) with A anti-Hermitian), d/dt 1/2 ||A^{q(t)}||^2_{2,h}|_0 = -<delta_h A, xi>_{2,h}, ||a||^2_{2,h} = h^d sum_{mu,x} <a_mu(x),a_mu(x)>, delta_h A = -sum_mu D^-_mu A_mu; uses <A, K(h ad_A) v> = <A, v> (pairing_halfCoth, the paper's K^*A = A) and summation by parts. Non-vacuity: gauge_hypotheses_nonvacuous (any field with ||h A_mu(x)|| <= 1/8, e.g. A = 0, has invertible J's and a local logarithm chart; exists_log_chart). All cited declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

lem:native-FP-inverse.title: Uniform transverse inverse
lem:native-FP-inverse.note: Proved on the periodic grid (Z/n)^iota with card iota = 4 (any n >= 1, mesh h > 0, side L = n h). Encoding: the Lie algebra is a finite-dimensional nontrivial real inner product space E with an arbitrary continuous bilinear bracket br (invariance of the metric and the Jacobi identity are not needed, so this is more general than the paper); K(Z) = (Z/2)coth(Z/2) is encoded through the paper identity K(Z) = 1/2 J(Z)^{-1}(I + e^Z) with J(Z) = sum_k Z^k/(k+1)! = int_0^1 e^{tZ} dt (eq:native-JK; OperatorHalfCoth.halfCoth, an analytic function, Z J(Z) = e^Z - 1 (mul_dexpJ), scalar check halfCoth z (e^z - 1) = (z/2)(e^z + 1) (halfCoth_real_mul), K(0) = I, ||K(Z) - I|| <= 12||Z||^2 on ||Z|| <= 1/4 (norm_halfCoth_sub_one_le)); M_A xi = delta_h(K(h ad_{A_mu}) D^+_mu xi + [A_mu, m_mu xi]) with delta_h = -sum D^-_mu (FaddeevPopov.fpOp, eq:native-FP). With r_FP = 1/(64(||br||+1)), independent of n and h, and the hypothesis ||A_mu||_{4,h} < r_FP for every direction mu (implied by the paper hypothesis ||A||_{4,h} < r_FP for the pointwise norm): fp_coercive: <M_A xi, xi>_{2,h} >= 1/2 ||D^+ xi||^2_{2,h} on the mean-zero space Z_h (eq:native-FP-coercivity; proof as in the paper: h||A||_inf <= ||A||_{4,h}, ||K - I|| <= C h^2|A|^2, weighted Hoelder L^4 x L^4 x L^2, ||m xi||_4 <= ||xi||_4, mean-zero Sobolev grid_sobolev_poincare_meanZero_l2); fp_bijective: M_A : Z_h -> Z_h bijective (exists unique mean-zero solution); fp_dual_inverse_sSup: ||D^+ M_A^{-1} f||_{2,h} <= 2 ||f||_{H^{-1}_h} with the dual norm defined as the sSup over mean-zero zeta with ||D^+ zeta||_{2,h} = 1 (dualNorm, abs_gridInner_le_dualNorm) (eq:native-FP-dual-inverse); fp_divergence_inverse: ||M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{2,h} + ||M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{4,h} + ||D^+ M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{2,h} <= (2 + 2 sqrt2 L + 4(3 + 2 sqrt2)) ||R||_{2,h} (eq:native-FP-divergence-inverse; constant independent of n for the fixed box L = 2 pi); fp_inverse_contDiffOn: on {A : ||A_mu||_{4,h} < r_FP} the extension N_A xi = M_A(xi - mean xi) + mean xi is invertible, A -> N_A^{-1} is C^k for every k (smooth and analytic orders), and N_A^{-1} f is the mean-zero solution of M_A xi = f for mean-zero f (smooth dependence of the inverse). Non-vacuity: example with A = 0 (M_0 = delta_h D^+). No self-adjointness of M_A is used. All cited declarations use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

thm:finite-Coulomb-normalization.title: Finite critical Coulomb normalization
thm:finite-Coulomb-normalization.note: Proved for the paper's exact gauge group G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (eq:gauge-group): StandardModelCoulomb.finite_coulomb_normalization_SM. Setting: 4D periodic grid (ZMod n)^iota, card iota = 4, mesh h, box side L = n h GENERAL (the paper fixes L = 2pi; constants depend only on L and the group/metric, never on n or h); A_SM = M3(C) x M2(C) with operator norms, invariant Frobenius metric Re tr(X3^*Y3) + Re tr(X2^*Y2) (toESM). Statement: for every eps_* > 0 there are eps_c, C_c > 0 such that every g_SM-valued seed B (skew-Hermitian blocks, tr B3 + tr B2 = 0) with ||B||_{4,h} + ||F_h(B)||_{2,h} <= eps_c admits a site gauge q with q_x in S(U(3)xU(2)) (unitary, det q3 * det q2 = 1) such that A = h^-1 Log(q_x e^{hB} q_{x+mu}^*) (linkA h B 1 q; FiniteCoulomb.linkA_at_one) is g_SM-valued (skew, tr A3 + tr A2 = 0), delta_h A = 0, ||A||_{1,h} + ||A||_{4,h} <= C_c(||B||_{2,h} + ||F_h(B)||_{2,h} + ||B||_{4,h}^2) and ||A||_{4,h} <= eps_*. NORM CONVENTION (disclosed): ||A||_{4,h} := sum_mu ||A_mu||_{4,h} (equivalent within fixed factors to the l4 combination of the components), ||A||_{2,h}^2 = sum_mu ||A_mu||_{2,h}^2, ||A||_{1,h} as in lem:native-reconstruction-identification, ||F||_{2,h} over mu<nu. Proof: general theorem FiniteCoulomb.finite_coulomb_normalization (unitary group of any finite-dim C*-algebra with invariant metric; the paper's homotopy ODE q' = xi q, xi = M_{A_s}^-1 delta_h R_s, Coulomb preservation, L^2 energy bound, curvature covariance + exact split, a priori a <= C_0 b + C_1 a^2, first exit, global existence via ODEContinuation.exists_solution_of_apriori); trace constraint along the path (CoulombTrace.trace_linkA_of_solution with tau = Re/Im(tr3 + tr2)) gives tr A3 + tr A2 = 0; then det(e^{hA}) = e^{tau(hA)} = 1 (MatrixDetExp.det_exp_eq_complex_exp_trace) on every link gives chi(q_x) chi(q_{x+mu})^* = 1 for chi = det3*det2, so chi(q) is a constant unit d, and the constant central phase c (c^5 = d^-1) gives the gauge c q in S(U(3)xU(2)) with the same links (the determinant clause is obtained by this post-hoc central correction rather than a Liouville ODE along the path; same conclusion). Also: U(N) (FrobeniusCoulomb), SU(N) (SpecialUnitaryCoulomb), general trace-constrained version (CoulombTrace); non-vacuity: FrobeniusCoulomb.exists_coulomb_zero_seed. Log = analytic series branch near 1 (conjugation-invariant chart).

prop:rooted-gauge-certificate.title: Rooted same-record gauge certificate
prop:rooted-gauge-certificate.note: PROVED. Certificate invariance and the Coulomb clause as before (RootedCertificate.rootedCertificate_gauge, RootedCoulomb.rooted_coulomb_normalization; the normalizing gauge g_x = q_x C_x is a unitary site gauge). NEW clauses (a)-(c) for this manuscript's common action eq:native-local-action = NativeDensity.localAction, for EVERY site gauge g with values in the gauge group G (in particular the normalizing one), on the admissible logarithm chart of the plaquettes. NativeGauge.CovData extends NativeDensity.Data with the manuscript's standing representation-packet assumptions (G inside the units, acting by norm-preserving conjugation; Ad-invariant ipA; rho_H(G)-invariant Higgs form; rho_S(g) commuting with sigma and gamma^a; covariant Yukawa blocks; unitary rho_S); action on records U -> g U g^-1 (realized in log coordinates by gaugeRecord), H -> rho_H(g) H, Psi -> rho_S(g) Psi, Psibar -> Psibar rho_S(g)^-1. (a) localAction_gauge, localSectors_gauge (each of the four sectors unchanged). (b) ipA_curv_gauge, hermH_hLink_gauge (literal curvature and Higgs-gradient packets), norm_intLink_gauge, norm_intLinkBar_gauge, graphNormSq_gauge (positive internal-link spinor graphs), wilsonModulus_gauge and its spinor/Higgs/curvature instances (Wilson moduli, both signs of m). (c) linkCov_gauge, massSq_tangentAct, covNorm_gauge, covNorm_record_gauge: the covector in the physical link tangent alpha = h^-1 Udot U^-1 transforms by the isometric tangent map, so its dual norm is unchanged; no derivative of the gauge appears. Non-vacuity: u1CovData (U(1), nontrivial group) with an explicit phase-rotation example; trivialCovData.

lem:determinant-screen-flux.title: Determinant compactness, admissibility, and flux
lem:determinant-screen-flux.note: All clauses proved (determinant_screen_flux) on the paper's periodic box of side L > 0 (2 pi in the paper), four-dimensional grids (Z/n_k)^4 with n_k -> infinity, h_k = L/n_k (oddness not needed). Hypotheses (structure CurvatureScreen, exactly the lemma's): G_SM links U_k; for every oriented pair mu<nu an arbitrary logarithm L_k(x,mu,nu) of the full plaquette (exp in both factors = P_{U,mu nu}(x); no chart and no bound on link logarithms assumed); literal full curvature packet F_k = (h^-2 L_k)_{mu<nu} bounded in L^2_h; full-box adjoint Wilson screen lim_{rho->0} limsup_k Omega_h(F;rho) = 0 used for positive displacements m h <= rho (implied by the paper's |m| h <= rho). Norm rendering: operator (unitarily invariant) norm on each matrix factor, max norm on pairs and on the six-component packet; equivalent to the invariant Euclidean metric up to a dimensional constant (boundedness/vanishing moduli unchanged); Ad acts by linear isometries (adPair, adPacket). Conclusions: (1) eventually f_h = l_c(F_h) exactly (eventually_detPacket; via eventual uniform smallness of h^2 F_h = L_h (eventually_small: scalar-magnitude uniform integrability from the proved thm:native-Wilson-compactness, exists_tail_le and the cell mass h^4) and DeterminantFlux.ellC_eq_arg_smChi); (2) eventually ||T_{mu,m} f - f||_{2,h} <= 2 ||W_{mu,m} F - F||_{2,h} for all mu, m >= 0 (Ad-invariance of l_c, ellC_openLink; |l_c| <= 2||.||), hence omega_h(f;rho) <= 2 Omega_h(F;rho) (negative ordinary shifts have the same norms by translation invariance); (3) max_{x,mu,nu} |phi_{mu nu,h}(x)| -> 0 (all ordered pairs, via abPhase_swap/abPhase_self); (4) R_h^0 f_h precompact in L^2 (TotallyBounded, unit-torus rendering of native_discrete_KR as for lem:native-discrete-KR); (5) eventually d_h f_h = 0 exactly (all cube sums vanish); (6) every coordinate-plane flux is 2 pi m, m integer (all k); eventually base-point independent, mean curvature L^-4 h^4 sum f = 2 pi m / L^2 and 2 pi |m| <= ||f_{mu nu}||_{2,h} (from determinant_screen_flux_exact / mean_curvature_eq_flux / two_pi_abs_flux_le); (7) the integer vectors (m_{mu nu,h})_{mu<nu} are bounded (2 pi |m| <= ||f|| <= 2||F||) and constant along a strictly increasing subsequence (pigeonhole, Finite.exists_infinite_fiber). Non-vacuity: curvatureScreen_trivial (trivial links, zero logarithms). Also closes prop:native-determinant-split (extra key, see there). All cited new declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

lem:determinant-Hodge-stability.title: Strong stability of the periodic discrete Hodge inverse
lem:determinant-Hodge-stability.note: Clause-level status: ALL CLAUSES PROVED. Finite identities and uniform bounds of eq:determinant-Hodge-bounds: GridHodge.hodge_stability_exact, hodge_stability_bounds (previous pass; closed zero-mean real two-form, d_h a0 = f, delta_h a0 = 0, mean zero, ||D+a0||_{2,h} = ||f||_{2,h}, L^-1||a0||_{2,h} + ||a0||_{4,h} <= (6+5 sqrt 2)||f||_{2,h} in four dimensions). Strong-convergence clause (this pass; unit-torus rendering, mesh h = 1/N - the paper's box is its dilation, and scaledPrimitive is linear so constant rescalings commute; real forms complexified by realC): if the zero-mean real two-forms f_h satisfy R_h^0 f_h -> F strongly in L^2 (componentwise), then for a0_h = delta_h Delta_h^dagger f_h = GridHodge.scaledPrimitive (1/N) f_h: R_h^0 a0_h -> a0 = delta Delta^dagger F strongly in L^2 (contPrimitive, the Fourier form a0^_nu(m) = sum_kappa conj(2 pi i m_kappa) F^_{kappa nu}(m)/(4 pi^2|m|^2)), a0 in H^1 and R_h^0 D+_mu a0_h -> d_mu a0 (weak derivative) strongly in L^2, I_h^trig a0_h -> a0 strongly in H^1 (hodge_strong_convergence, any dimension), and in four dimensions R_h^0 a0_h -> a0 strongly in L^4 (hodge_strong_convergence_four). Proof as in the paper: the DFT multiplier of delta_h Delta_h^dagger (coef_scaledPrimitive: conj(sym_kappa)/sum_i|sym_i|^2, from dft_realC_bwd, dft_realC_lap, dft_realC_lapInv) is bounded by 1/4 and that of each first difference by 1 (norm_hodgeMult_le, norm_sym_mul_hodgeMult_le), both converge at fixed frequency (tendsto_hodgeMult); raw L^2 convergence of f_h gives l^2 convergence of the coefficients (vanishing tail), bounded multipliers preserve it, and lem:native-reconstruction-identification (proved this pass) gives the L^4 and H^1 conclusions. No closedness of f_h is needed for the convergence clause (only zero mean). Non-vacuity example with f = 0 (and the exact identities of the previous pass are non-vacuous on explicit curls).

prop:periodic-determinant-normalization.title: Zero-flux Abelian normalization with unrestricted flat holonomy
prop:periodic-determinant-normalization.note: Clause-level status: ALL CLAUSES PROVED. Exact part (previous pass): DeterminantFlux.periodic_determinant_normalization_exact (potential a0 = delta_h Delta_h^dagger f, constants with L c_mu in (-pi, pi] equal to the principal arguments of the cycle holonomies of the flat residual, periodic site gauge, delta_h(a0 + c) = 0; no smallness of f, a0 or cycle phases used) and, for screened sequences, DeterminantScreenFlux.native_determinant_split. Sequence clauses (this pass, DeterminantNormalizationSequence): for a screened bounded-curvature sequence (DeterminantScreenFlux.CurvatureScreen: bounded literal full curvature in L^2_h and vanishing adjoint Wilson modulus, box of side L, h = L/n_k) with zero determinant flux for all large k, and any constants c_h with |L c_{mu,h}| <= pi (in particular those of the exact normalization), precompact_sequence: every subsequence of the coordinates a_h = a0_h + c_h has a further subsequence along which (in the unit-torus rendering, coordinates a'_h = L a_h, forward differences Dp = L D+_h, reconstructions on T^4 = dilation of the box) R_h^0 a_h converges strongly in L^4 and L^2, R_h^0 D+_mu a_h converges strongly in L^2 (to the weak derivatives of the limit), and I_h^trig a_h converges strongly in H^1 (sequential strong precompactness); tendsto_mesh_mul_sup: h ||a_h||_{inf,h} -> 0 for the whole sequence (each component), so the coordinates are eventually principal. Proof as in the paper: lem:determinant-screen-flux (determinant_screen_flux, proved: L^2 precompactness of R_h^0 f_h, eventual smallness of the phases, zero mean from zero flux via detCurvature_closed_meanZero), the strong-convergence clause of lem:determinant-Hodge-stability (HodgeStrongConvergence.hodge_strong_convergence, proved this pass; components of the packet limit extended antisymmetrically, curvLimit, tendsto_curv_components), extraction of the bounded constants (tendsto_subseq_of_bounded), lem:native-reconstruction-identification (proved this pass) for the L^4 and H^1 statements, eq:native-link-coeff (NativeCriticalGrid.tendsto_meshSup) along every subsequence and the subsequence principle tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto for h||a||_inf -> 0. Non-vacuity: the trivial screened sequence (DeterminantScreenFlux.curvatureScreen_trivial) has zero flux (planeFlux_detLinks_trivial).

prop:native-determinant-split.title: Exact determinant normalization and semisimple remainder
prop:native-determinant-split.note: EXTRA KEY (not in batch e7; closed as a corollary of lem:determinant-screen-flux, now proved). DeterminantScreenFlux.native_determinant_split: for a screened sequence (CurvatureScreen, see lem:determinant-screen-flux) whose determinant flux vanishes for all large k, for all large k (h = L/n_k) the remaining admissibility input of DeterminantFlux.native_determinant_split_exact is discharged: |Arg chi(P_U)| < pi/3 and logarithms of ALL oriented plaquettes (extLog: L_{nu mu} = -L_{mu nu}, L_{mu mu} = 0, exp = P since P_{nu mu} = P_{mu nu}^-1) with entries <= c0, 2 c0 < min(pairChart, pi), eventually (eventually_small). Hence, eventually, with the paper's potential a0 = delta_h Delta_h^dagger f (prop:periodic-determinant-normalization, exact construction, proved) there are constants c (L c in (-pi,pi]) and real site lifts t with: the Abelian normalization and delta_h(a0+c) = 0; l_c(L) = h^2 f; V = e^{-haZ_c} U^{e^{tZ_c}} in G_ss exactly (chi = 1, det = 1); P_{U'} = e^{h^2 f Z_c} P_V; the chart logarithm of P_V is Pi_ss L, i.e. F_h(V) = Pi_ss F_h(U') (eq:determinant-semisimple-curvature); Ad V = Ad U'; lift changes t -> t + 2 pi k give the central G_ss gauge z6^k (rooted certificate unchanged: RootedWilson.splitLinks_rootedWord_lift_change, previously proved). New clause proved: the semisimple curvature screen of V is bounded by c_ss = 1 + 2||Z_c|| times the full screen of U, for every mu, m and every lifts/potential (ss_screen_le: Ad V = Ad U since central factors act trivially in Ad (adLinks_splitLinks), Pi_ss is Ad-equivariant and commutes with the open adjoint links (piSSOp_openLink), ||Pi_ss X|| <= c_ss ||X||). Corollary policy: only the exact construction of prop:periodic-determinant-normalization is used (its open sequence-compactness clauses are not). Non-vacuity: curvatureScreen_trivial with planeFlux_trivial. Axioms: standard only.

lem:flat-semisimple-normalization.title: Flat semisimple normalization without a small-holonomy assumption
lem:flat-semisimple-normalization.note: Proved on the periodic four-dimensional grid (Z/n)^4 (any n >= 1, mesh h > 0, box side L = n h), G_ss = SU(3) x SU(2) (Gss). Flatness: every oriented plaquette trivial, V_mu(x)V_nu(x+mu) = V_nu(x)V_mu(x+nu) (IsFlat). Part A (any group): ladder lemmas (plaquette moves along lines and staircases), flatness implies the based cycle holonomies w_mu = V_mu(0)V_mu(e_mu)...V_mu((n-1)e_mu) commute (cycle_commute); flat_gauge_equiv: two flat periodic fields with equal based cycle holonomies are gauge equivalent by the explicit site gauge g_x = P_W(x)^-1 P_V(x) comparing staircase path transports from the root (exactly the paper's argument: plaquette moves preserve the comparison, equal cycle holonomies make it periodic; no pointwise-ratio flatness assumed); flat_gauge_eq_const for constant commuting targets. Part B (no simultaneous spectral theorem needed): a common eigenvector of finitely many commuting complex operators (exists_common_eigenvector, by invariant-subspace induction); for commuting U_mu in SU(N): b_mu = cfc(i arg)(U_mu) - 2 pi i k_mu P with P the rank-one projector onto a common eigenvector, k_mu = tr(cfc(i arg)U_mu)/(2 pi i) in Z (det exp = exp tr), giving pairwise commuting, anti-Hermitian, traceless logarithms with e^{b_mu} = U_mu and ||b_mu|| <= (N+1) pi (operator norm) (exists_commuting_logs) -- this is the paper's 'subtract 2 pi m from one eigenangle' rendered via the common eigenvector. Assembly flat_semisimple_normalization: V flat => there are commuting b_mu = (b^3_mu, b^2_mu) in su(3)+su(2) (anti-Hermitian, traceless), entrywise |b_mu(i,j)| <= 4 pi / L uniformly, with cycle holonomies e^{L b_mu} equal to those of V, and an SU(3)xSU(2) site gauge g with g_x V_mu(x) g_{x+mu}^-1 = e^{h b_mu} for all x, mu; no smallness of the holonomies. flat_semisimple_normalization_seq: for grids n_k with fixed L = n_k h_k, the bounds are uniform in k and after extraction the constant coordinates converge (constant_coordinates_subseq, Bolzano-Weierstrass); constant coordinates have identically zero first differences and constant commuting links have trivial plaquettes (plaq_const_eq_one), hence zero curvature. Non-vacuity: isFlat_one. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

cor:determinant-resolved-closure.title: Determinant-resolved finite Wilson closure
cor:determinant-resolved-closure.note: PROVED (e40), both forms, G_SM = S(U(3) x U(2)) in M3(C) x M2(C), unit-torus rendering (box side L = 1, h = 1/N, as thm:finite-Wilson-zero-defect). determinant_resolved_closure_SM (certificate form): there are cutoff-independent eps_c, eps_* > 0 such that for records with internal links U_h = e^{hA_h} in G_SM (plaquettes in the log chart), (F1), (F3), (F4), (F5) exactly as in finite_wilson_zero_defect_SM, zero determinant flux for all large k (planeFlux of det U_2), and the semisimple remainder V_h = e^{-h a_h Z_c} e^{t_h Z_c} U_h e^{-t_h Z_c} (splitVg, matrix form of DeterminantSplit.splitLinks) built from the paper's potential a_h = delta_h Delta_h^dagger f_h + c_h (detCoord, |c_h| <= pi) and site phases t_h having an admissible rooted seed, plaquettes in the chart and rooted certificate <= eps_c (eq:semisimple-only-certificate): actual G_SM site gauges g_h = q_h e^{t_h Z_c} act on the same records, the normalized connection is exactly A_h = b_h + Z_c a_h with delta_h b_h = 0 and ||b_h||_{4,h} <= eps_* (only b_h small: no smallness of the determinant curvature, of ||a_h||_4, or of the flat cycle holonomies), eventually delta_h a_h = 0 and delta_h A_h = 0 (eq:determinant-combined-connection), and after extraction ALL conclusions of thm:finite-Wilson-zero-defect: eq:Wilson-strong-convergence (strong L4 convergence of the full, non-small A_h = B + a_0 Z_c, F = F_A with no mixed commutator), eq:native-all-sector-limit, reconstructed-field consistency, the distributional Einstein-SM equations, strong L1 bosonic stresses. determinant_resolved_closure_flat_SM: the exact-flatness alternative (V_h G_ss-valued, i.e. chi(V_h) = 1 = the determinant normalization equation, and all plaquettes of V_h trivial; no smallness of any holonomy): A_h = beta_h + Z_c a_h with constant commuting bounded beta_h (lem:flat-semisimple-normalization) and the same conclusions. Proof = the paper's: generic extraction with a central background (DeterminantResolvedExtraction: Ad e^{h(b+aZ)} = Ad e^{hb}; isometric-link Wilson compactness needs only a bounded L2 full connection; curvature split F(b+aZ) = F(b) + fZ on the chart once h||a||_inf -> 0; semisimple compactness from thm:native-discrete-Coulomb or from constant commuting links; combined_criterion_core = all conclusions), the remainder normalization and its transfer (determinant_resolved_post / _of_rootedNorm, generic in a C*-algebra with a central skew direction), and prop:periodic-determinant-normalization via the record->CurvatureScreen bridge (curvatureScreen_of_records, then DeterminantNormalizationSequence.precompact_sequence). Disclosed renderings: (a) eps_c is the threshold of the G_SM rooted normalization (rootedNorm_SM) applied to the G_ss-valued remainder (G_ss in G_SM); the statement asserts a cutoff-independent threshold; (b) the site phases t_h are arbitrary in the certificate form (the paper's t_h with chi(V_h) = 1 is a special case; the normalization equation is assumed only in the flat form, where V_h must be G_ss-valued); (c) 'for all sufficiently small h' is rendered by hypotheses for all k except zero flux (eventually), i.e. after reindexing the tail; (d) the full-plaquette log chart ||P_U - 1|| < 1 is assumed (it defines the literal packet F_h, as in the Lean rendering of thm:finite-Wilson-zero-defect); (e) matter representations as in thm:finite-Wilson-zero-defect (NativeDensity.Data). Standard axioms only. Non-vacuity: const_background_hyps (a constant potential a = c of ANY size satisfies the background hypotheses of the extraction), splitVg_trivial (trivial split data give V = 1: G_ss-valued, flat, certificate 0), and the bCompact_of_const example.

lem:covariant-quadrature.title: Covariant cell-average quadrature
lem:covariant-quadrature.note: Proved (e19). Setting: metric connection D = d + omega on the trivialised bundle [0,1]^d x V, V a real Hilbert space (the manuscript's finite direct sum of test fibres), omega : R^d -> L(R^d, End V) with skew-adjoint values (IsMetric), covariant derivative covDeriv omega X x = dX(x) + omega(x)(.) X(x); uniform grid of mesh h = 1/M with cells C_x = x + [0,h)^d (UnitCubeRiemannSum.cell); P_{x<-y} the parallel transport (PathOrderedExp.IsTransport: P' = -omega(gamma)(gamma') P, P(0) = 1) along a path gamma_{x,y} from y to the node x; Q_h v(x) = h^-d int_{C_x} P_{x<-y} v(y) dy (cellAverage, eq:covariant-test-average). (a) abs_covariant_quadrature_sub_le (eq:covariant-quadrature): for any path family with speed <= l, a measurable transport field y -> P_{x<-y}, X continuous on the cube and differentiable along the paths with ||DX|| <= B there, and integrable v: |h^d sum_x <X(x), Q_h v(x)> - int <X, v>| <= l B ||v||_{L^1}; the proof is the paper's (metric compatibility makes transports isometries, inner_transport_apply_apply; covariant FTC along the path, abs_inner_covariant_ftc: |<X(x), P_{x<-y} w> - <X(y), w>| <= B l ||w||). (b) abs_covariant_quadrature_straight_sub_le: the concrete family of straight segments inside the cell (length < h in the sup norm, so C = 1) for omega bounded and Lipschitz on the cube; existence of the transports by gluing short Picard-Lindelof pieces (exists_transport_of_le) and Lipschitz dependence on y by Gronwall (norm_straightTransport_sub_le), so the measurability hypothesis is discharged. (c) Norm bounds: norm_cellAverage_le (||Q_h v||_{inf,h} <= ||v||_inf, with a pointwise bound on the cell) and cellAverage_sq_sum_le (h^d sum_x ||Q_h v(x)||^2 <= int ||v||^2, Cauchy-Schwarz on each cell, sq_setIntegral_le_mul); straight_cellAverage_norm_bounds packages both for the straight family. (d) Equivariance: isTransport_gaugeTransform (endpoint transformation: g(gamma t) P(t) g(gamma 0)^-1 is the transport of omega^g = g omega g^-1 - (dg) g^-1), cellAverage_gaugeTransform (Q'_h(g v) = g Q_h v) and inner_cellAverage_gaugeTransform (both sides of eq:covariant-quadrature unchanged under unitary frame changes, LinearIsometryEquiv-valued g). Disclosed renderings: buffered chart = unit cube (any coordinate box is an affine image); trivialised bundle (fixed local frames, as in the manuscript); lengths and operator norms in the sup norm of R^d (other norms change C by a dimensional factor); 'a fixed family of paths' = a path family with measurable transport field (automatic for the straight family). Non-vacuity: flat-connection example at the end of the file.

prop:equivariant-native-budgets.title: Equivariant native first-variation budgets
prop:equivariant-native-budgets.note: PROVED in full (e40), unit periodic box rendering ([0,1]^4, grid (Z/n)^4, h = 1/n). EquivariantBudgets.equivariant_native_budgets: for a covariant packet C (fixed coefficient bank C.toData), fixed coercive link/matter metrics M, a compact oriented coframe chart K_e, an amplitude bound A and a band constant B there are C_0 >= 0, c_res > 0 such that for every K >= 1 and n with hK <= c_res, every smooth Z^4-periodic field tuple z with coframes in K_e, |z| <= A and the growing-band bounds ||D^j z|| <= B K^j (j <= 3; eq:eq-growing-band, q >= 5 only strengthens it), and every C^1 periodic physical test v = (k, a, eta_H, eta_Psi, eta_Psibar): eq:eq-native-consistency |D S_h^loc(S_h z)[I_h^cov v] - D S(z)[v]| <= C_0 h K^3 n_z(v) and eq:eq-native-stationarity |D S_h^loc(S_h z)[I_h^cov v]| <= C_0 sigma_h^link n_z(v); hence c_h^eq <= C h B^3, eps_h^eq <= C sigma_h^link (eq:eq-native-budgets); the exact site-gauge invariance of sigma_h^link is NativeLinkCov.covNormP_record_gauge (proved earlier). Encodings: D S(z)[v] = contVar L0 z v~_z, the first variation of the continuum action int L0(J^1 z) with L0 = limDensity firstJetDensity (the Einstein-SM Lagrangian identified sector by sector in NativeEulerConsistency); v~_z = liftTest z v (symmetric coframe lift liftM, eq:metric-lift; other components unchanged); I_h^cov v = Icov n z v = Q_h v~_z (cell average = the covariant average of lem:covariant-quadrature for the flat positive comparison connection, which the proposition allows); n_z(v) = testSize (eq:equivariant-test-size literally: ||k||_{W^{1,inf}} via partial derivatives, sup norms of a, eta's, L^2 norms of D_A a, D_A eta_H, nabla^{ref,A} eta_Psi, nabla^{ref,A} eta_Psibar, flat reference spin connection); sigma_h^link = covNormP. Proof = the manuscript's: periodic continuum integration by parts (contVar_eq_integral_contEuler), D S_h^loc = h^4 sum E_h^raw (fderiv_eq_sum_eulerRow), the pointwise O(hK^3) Euler-row consistency (NativeEulerConsistency.native_consistency) paired with the averaged test via Jensen (sum_norm_cellAvg_le), the cell quadrature against X = E_0 (abs_quadrature_sub_le) with ||D E_0|| <= C K^3 (native_euler_lipschitz = eq:eq-euler-jets, via ContEulerBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_eulerOp_le and the native scaling NativeTail.Rfull_scale), ||v~_z|| <= max(K_l,1) n_z(v) (norm_liftTest_le), and for stationarity NativeLinkCov.abs_deriv_localAction_le with ||Q_h v~||_{0,h} <= sqrt 8 sup||v~|| (the chart conditions follow from native_consistency and h|A| <= 1/512). Disclosed renderings: periodic unit box and periodic C^1 tests instead of the buffered chart with compactly supported smooth tests; flat comparison/reference connections; a fixed bank. Non-vacuity: const_field_hyps (constant field tuples satisfy the field hypotheses with B = 0). Note: the file imports the NativeTail* modules (Continuum/NativeTailStructure, NativeTailTransfer, NativeTailTransferBounds).

prop:Wilson-packet-transfer.title: Finite packet and open-link transfer
prop:Wilson-packet-transfer.note: All three clauses PROVED (e28), in a complete normed real algebra with ||1|| = 1 (represented gauge algebra) acting on fibres; standard axioms only. (a) eq:Wilson-packet-consistency with the SHARP rate h B^2: for the literal exponential links U = e^{hA} of the nodal record of the reconstructed connection (the reconstruction interpolates the record), the literal log-plaquette F^h_{mu nu} = h^-2 log(e^{hA_mu(x)} e^{hA_nu(x+he_mu)} e^{-hA_mu(x+he_nu)} e^{-hA_nu(x)}) (analytic branch, ShiftedPlaquette.logOneAdd) satisfies |F^h - F_A(x)| <= curvC(c) h B^2, F_A = d_mu A_nu - d_nu A_mu + [A_mu,A_nu] (norm_fieldStrength_sub_curvature_le), and the literal Higgs packet K^h = h^-1(e^{h dRho(A_mu(x))}H(x+he_mu) - H(x)) satisfies |K^h - D_A H(x)| <= higgsC(c) h B^2 (norm_higgsPacket_sub_covDeriv_le); hypotheses = the |alpha| <= 2 part of eq:eq-growing-band on a convex chart S (|A|,|H| <= c, |DA|,|DH| <= cB, DA, DH cB^2-Lipschitz), B >= 1, 0 < h <= 1, hB <= c_res(c) (explicit cRes); every power of B is tracked (exponential-link normal form, products with absolute errors, sharp logarithm step), so the error is C h B^2 and not h poly(B). wilson_packet_consistency states both bounds at every node for the literal library packets NativeScaling.fieldStrength / NativeScaling.higgsLink of a grid record sampling the reconstruction (rho_H(e^{ha}) = e^{h drho(a)}). (b) eq:Wilson-transport-consistency in the manuscript's orientation: rho(U_{mu,m}(x)) = U(x)U(x+he)...U(x+(m-1)he) (openLinkPos) vs P^A_{mu,mh}(x) = transport from x+mhe back to x (backwardLink): ||.|| <= e^{2K mh}(mh) Lambda h e^{K mh+2Kh} = C rho0 h B (norm_openLinkPos_sub_backwardLink_le); negative m (inverse ordered product) = norm_invLink_sub_forwardLink_le; previous pointers kept. (c) eq:Wilson-finite-screen => eq:Wilson-continuum-screen: generic quantitative transfer (norm_transfer_pos_le / _neg_le: for x in the cell of node x0 and |s| = mh + r, 0 <= r <= h, |T_sY(x) - Y(x) - (W_{+-m}Y^d(x0) - Y^d(x0))| <= X^4 h (K + 3 Lambda T) M_Y + X(3 L_Y h + 2 eps), with transport base-point/length Lipschitz bounds and (b)), exact cell quadrature eLpNorm_le_of_cellwise (L^2(Q) <= (h^d sum_nodes |G|^2)^{1/2} + eta |Q|^{1/2}), and the asymptotic wilson_continuum_screen; instantiated for the literal packets: wilson_packet_transfer_curvature (rho = Ad: exp(h ad A)Z = e^{hA} Z e^{-hA}, exp_adCLM_apply via Mathlib map_exp; rho(U_m)Y = U_m Y U_m^{-1} for both signs, openLinkPos_adCLM_apply / invLink_adCLM_apply; band => |F_A| <= (2c+2c^2)B, Lip F_A <= (2c+4c^2)B^2) and wilson_packet_transfer_higgs (links e^{h a}, a = drho_H(A); band => same for D_A H). Rendering (disclosed): coordinate chart = R^iota (any finite iota; 4 in the paper) with Lebesgue measure and sup norm, nodes h Z^iota; the finite modulus Omega_h is the sum over every finite set of nodes x of Q' with x + m h e_mu in Q' (= the paper's Q'_{h,mu,m}), all mu, 0 < |m|h <= rho; 'lim_rho limsup_h = 0' in the eps-rho-eventually form; conclusion on any bounded measurable chart Q whose (rho0+1)-neighbourhood lies in Q', all mu, all |s| <= rho, L^2(Q) norm of covTransport(x,s)Y(x+se) - Y(x) (covTransport = P^A_{mu,s}, both signs); the growing band is assumed for the reconstructed fields on the whole coordinate space (the reconstructions are global periodic trigonometric polynomials on the comparison box), only |alpha| <= 2 of it is used; transports exist for every length (CovariantQuadrature.exists_transport_of_le). Non-vacuity: zero connection / constant packets satisfy every hypothesis.

lem:translation-Kato.title: Translation Kato inequality
lem:translation-Kato.note: translation_kato: for a Hilbert fibre H over R or C, any representation rho : G -> H ->L H with values in unitary (H ->L H), parallel transports P x : G and displacement a (= s e_mu) in an additive group of points, | |Y(x+a)| - |Y(x)| | <= |T Y(x) - Y(x)| with T Y(x) = rho(P x)(Y(x+a)) (eq:continuum-covariant-translation). The 'thus' clause: translation_kato_eLpNorm (the L^p, in particular L^2, ordinary translation modulus of |Y| is bounded by the covariant one, any measure) and translation_kato_modulus_tendsto (vanishing covariant modulus forces vanishing ordinary modulus).

lem:compact-magnitude-ui.title: Compact scalar magnitude implies energy uniform integrability
lem:compact-magnitude-ui.note: Proved. For a family F : ι → Lp V 2 (μ.restrict K) (V any normed group) that is relatively compact (compactMagnitude_ui_of_isCompact_closure: IsCompact (closure (range F))) or totally bounded (compactMagnitude_ui), eq:compact-magnitude-ui holds in the form CriticalCurvatureUI μ K F of Continuum/CriticalCurvatureUniformIntegrabilityExact.lean: sup_f sup_{E ⊆ K measurable, μ E ≤ δ} ∫⁻_E ‖f‖² → 0 as δ ↓ 0. Proof as in the paper: finite L² net of radius ε/2, MeasureTheory.unifIntegrable_finite for the net (absolute continuity), and the triangle inequality ‖1_E f‖₂ ≤ ‖f − f_j‖₂ + ‖1_E f_j‖₂ (compactMagnitude_unifIntegrable gives UnifIntegrable F 2 μ in Mathlib's sense). The finite-measure hypothesis on K is not needed and is not assumed (strictly more general).

prop:Wilson-screen-compactness.title: Covariant screen compactness at the critical endpoint
prop:Wilson-screen-compactness.note: PROVED (e28), all three assertions, unit-torus rendering of the periodic comparison box (as for thm:native-Wilson-compactness): the chart B is an open subset of T^d = UnitAddTorus d (any finite d) with Haar probability measure, coordinate displacements t -> t + coordPt mu s. Fibre F a finite-dimensional real normed space; rho(P_{mu,s}(t)) linear isometries (unitary representation). Hypotheses exactly the paper's: Y_h bounded in L^2(B) (a.e.-strongly measurable on the box) and eq:Wilson-continuum-screen (CovScreen: on every compact K in B, for every eps a delta with, cofinitely in h, ||T_{mu,s}Y_h - Y_h||_{L^2(K)} <= eps for all mu and 0 <= s <= delta; only positive displacements are used). Conclusions: (i) |Y_h| relatively compact in L^2_loc(B) (wilson_screen_magnitude_nets: on every compact K in B finite eps-nets in L^2(K) drawn from the family; equivalent total-boundedness form LocalKRTorus.totallyBounded_of_nets), via the translation Kato inequality (lem:translation-Kato, translation_kato_of_isometry) and the new LOCAL Kolmogorov-Riesz theorem LocalKRTorus.exists_net_of_local_modulus (Lipschitz cutoff chi = max(0,1-dist(.,K)/r) with cthickening 3r K in B, translation modulus of chi f bounded by the local modulus on cthickening 2r K plus (s/r)||f||, torus Kolmogorov-Riesz kolmogorovRiesz_torus_vector_cofinite); (ii) |Y_h|^2 uniformly integrable on every compact K in B (wilson_screen_magnitude_ui: for every eps a delta with ||Y_h||_{L^2(E)} <= eps for all h and measurable E in K with |E| <= delta), via lem:compact-magnitude-ui (compactMagnitude_ui, proved); (iii) vector part (wilson_screen_vector_nets): if the transports are the unitary parallel transports of continuous represented connections a_h (IsUnitaryTransport: rho(P) is the two-sided inverse of the unitary forward transport of tau -> a_h(t + tau e_mu)) with sup_h ||a_h||_{L^4(B)} <= M_A (eq:critical-A4-bound, connections in the normalized local gauge), then Y_h itself is relatively compact in L^2_loc(B). Proof as the paper: eq:short-line-integral ||rho(P)-I|| <= min(2, int_0^s |a(t+tau e)|) (IsUnitaryTransport.norm_sub_one_le, from the integral equation and unitarity), Fubini |int_K L_s| <= s ||a||_{L^1(K'')} <= s M_A (Holder L^4 -> L^1 on the probability torus), Chebyshev |{L_s > delta}| <= s M_A/delta, uniform integrability (ii) on the translated exceptional set, continuity of the transports in the base point (Gronwall + uniform continuity) for measurability, then local Kolmogorov-Riesz.

lem:critical-Coulomb-Hodge.title: Critical Coulomb Hodge absorption
lem:critical-Coulomb-Hodge.note: Proved in the box rendering (as for prop:orlicz): the small-energy Coulomb ball B is a coordinate box Q = box a b in R^4, and B' compactly contained in B is rendered by an arbitrary compact K in Q (L^4(K) convergence for every compact K covers every B' with closure in B). Connections: m x m complex-matrix-valued one-forms with entries A_h nu c e in W^{1,2}(Q) (implicit in the lemma: the Coulomb representatives of prop:critical-uhlenbeck are W^{1,2}; needed to make d^*A and F_A functions; no uniform W^{1,2} bound is assumed), co-closed = sum_mu d_mu A_mu = 0 a.e. on Q, F = dA + [A ^ A] entrywise from the weak gradients (curvatureW), L^p norms entrywise. critical_coulomb_hodge_box: there is delta_0 > 0 depending ONLY on the dimension and m (not on Q or on the cutoff; delta_0 = (2 kappa + 1)^{-1}, kappa = coulombKappa built from Mathlib's Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev constant) such that if all L^4(Q) entry norms of A_h and A are <= delta <= delta_0 ('uniformly sufficiently small'), A_h -> A in L^2(Q) and F_{A_h} -> F_A in L^2(Q), then A_h -> A in L^4(K) for every compact K in Q (eq:critical-A4-strong). Proof as in the manuscript: chi in C_c^infty(Q), chi = 1 near K; compactly supported Hodge estimate for chi a_h (flat Weitzenboeck identity ||grad w||^2 = 1/2 sum ||(dw)_{mu nu}||^2 + ||d^*w||^2 for compactly supported W^{1,2} one-forms, weitzenbock_flat, proved by periodisation to the flat torus, the Fourier rule for weak derivatives and a Lagrange identity on every Fourier mode) and critical Sobolev H^1_c -> L^4; d^*(chi a_h) is of order zero by co-closedness (eLpNorm_div_cutoff_le); d(chi a_h) = chi(F_{A_h} - F_A) - ([chi a, A_h] + [A, chi a]) + dchi ^ a_h (curl_cutoff_eq); absorption of the delta-terms when kappa delta <= 1/2 (coulomb_hodge_step). Non-vacuity example in CriticalGaugeEstimates.lean.

prop:native-consistency.title: Growing-band consistency of the unchanged finite action
prop:native-consistency.note: PROVED (e34, sorry-free, standard axioms). Both clauses. Setting: the unchanged local action S_h^loc = NativeDensity.localAction (all four rows of eq:native-densities: literal Cartan plaquette logarithm, gauge plaquettes, Higgs links, Dirac links) on the periodic grid (Z/n)^4 with mesh h; a smooth field tuple y : R^4 -> (e, A, H, Psi, Psibar) of period n h (the paper's periodic comparison box), sampled at the nodes (samp). Raw Euler row E_h^raw(y)(x) = h^-4 d_{y(x)} S_h^loc (DiscreteEulerConsistency.eulerRow, = eq:raw-euler-row in covector form). Continuum Euler density E_0 = Euler-Lagrange expression d_w L_0 - sum_mu d_mu d_{p_mu} L_0 (contEuler) of the continuum Lagrangian L_0(w,p) = F^(1)(0; w,...,w; p,...,p) (limDensity of the first-jet density of lem:native-firstjet-normal-form), identified sectorwise (limDensity_firstJetDensity_eq, nuFieldStrength_cont: F = dA - dA + [A,A]; nuHiggsLinkJet_cont: D_A H = dH + rho_H(A)H; nuDiracDiffJet_cont / nuDiracDiffBarJet_cont: spin-covariant derivatives with the torsion-free reader connection omega(e, de) and rho_S(A); gravity = first-order Palatini representative NativeGravityJet.palatiniFirstOrder, the convention of prop:native-gravity-firstjet; its Euler expression equals that of any density differing by a divergence). (1) eq:native-consistency = NativeEulerConsistency.native_consistency: for a compact coframe chart K_e in {det > 0} (uniform inverse metric), amplitude bound A and band constant B there are C and c_res > 0 such that for all K >= 1, h > 0 with hK <= c_res, all n and every C^3 field of period nh with coframe values in K_e, |y| <= A and ||D^j y|| <= B K^j (j = 1,2,3; eq:growing-derivatives at the orders used, q >= 5 only strengthens it), the samples lie on the oriented and Cartan-logarithm charts and ||E_h^raw(S_h y)(x) - E_0(y)(h x)|| <= C h K^3 at EVERY node. Proof = the paper's: exact jet scaling F^(1)(h,(v,Kq)) = K^2 G(K^-1, hK, (v,q)) (firstJetDensity_jetScale, lem:native-scaling on first jets, all four sectors) with G smooth at rho = 0 for every nu (contDiffAt_scaledDensity), uniform C^3 bounds on compact parameter/jet sets (exists_densityReg), the generic discrete-to-continuum Euler consistency of shifted-first-jet actions (norm_eulerRow_sub_contEuler_le: explicit discrete summation by parts eulerRow_action_eq, Taylor expansion of shifted stencils and of the divided difference of D_dF using symmetry of D^2 y, constant eulerConst independent of h, n and the field), and the exact rescalings of the raw row (eulerRow_smul_action) and of E_0 (contEuler_scale). (2) eq:native-Cartan = native_cartan_consistency: ||R^h_{mu nu}(x) - R_{mu nu}(z)|| <= C h K^3 for every node x and EVERY z in its cell (||z - h x|| <= h), R = d omega + omega wedge omega of the torsion-free reader connection omega_mu = e Gamma_mu e^-1 - d_mu e e^-1 (contCartan), which equals the Riemann tensor of g = e^T eta e in mixed frame/coordinate components e Riem_{mu nu}(g) e^-1 (contCartan_eq_riem: the Cartan structure equation, proved; riemMat = d_mu Gamma_nu - d_nu Gamma_mu + [Gamma_mu, Gamma_nu] with the Christoffel symbols readerGamma of g); native_cartan_riem states the clause directly against e Riem(g) e^-1. This is an L^infty bound for the piecewise-constant reconstruction, hence the L^2(Q) bound with factor |Q|^(1/2). Disclosed: finite-dimensional gauge algebra and Higgs/spinor fibres (FiniteDimensional, as in the paper); trivialised bundles, one fixed frame; sup norms on R^4 (other norms change C by dimensional factors); readerGamma is the Christoffel formula with dg = (de)^T eta e + e^T eta de (NativeScaling.readerG, product rule; not re-derived against Gravity/CoordinateCurvature.lean). Non-vacuity: example (flat constant field satisfies the packet). Fixed-scale corollary: native_sigma_of_solution.

thm:native-source.title: Leakage-tolerant physical forcing estimate
thm:native-source.note: PROVED (e41), all three displays, NativeSourceThm.native_source, on the paper's periodic native setting (odd grid (Z/n)^4, h=2pi/n, period-2pi auxiliary box, Sigma = T^3): slab Q=[t0,t1]x(0,2pi]^3 buffered by Q'=[t0-delta,t1+delta)x[0,2pi)^3 inside one period (delta<t0, t1+delta<=2pi). Conclusions: (1) eq:native-zero-source ||R_B(z_h)||_{L2(Q)}+||R_D(z_h)||_{L2(Q)} <= C eps_{0,h} (native_zero_source: native_consistency at the full field [growing reserve from Bernstein+measured tail, norm_iteratedFDeriv_recon_le], S_h z_h=u_h for odd n, lem:nodal-source-transfer with the Euler density derivative O(K^3) [exists_fderiv_Rfull_bound], lattice mass = grid mass [nodalMassSq_le_grid]); (2) eq:native-strong-source ||R_B||_{L2_tH^k_x}+||R_D||_{L2_tH^{k+1}_x} <= C F_{h,k} with the literal budget NativeRate.forcingBudget (any C_k>0), by native_source_assembly with: (h0) = (1); (h1),(h3) native_source_tail + triangle inequality for the slab norm (sobX_add_le, Minkowski); (h2) the strip/Bernstein step: the low-frequency rows have analytic (Gevrey-1) directional growth ||D^p R_B(z^lo)(v..v)|| <= C K^2 p!(RK)^p, ||D^p R_D(z^lo)|| <= C K p!(RK)^p (native_low_gevrey: the normalised density is C^omega/real-analytic on the chart [NativeDensityAnalytic], Euler rows = Phi(second jet) with Phi analytic [eulerOp_eq_phiE, foOp_eq_phiF], uniform power series on compacts + composition-series coefficient bounds [AnalyticGevrey.exists_gevrey_comp], Bernstein bounds for the rescaled head) -- this is the real-variable form of the paper's complex-strip bound (it yields the same Fourier decay |f^(t,l)| <= A e^{-a|l|/K}, GevreyFourier.norm_mFourierCoeff_le_of_gevrey, without complexification) -- then lem:log-source-upgrade in the slab norm (NativeSlab.sobX_log_upgrade: bridge 2pi-box Field/covector-valued objects -> scalar unit-torus Fourier slices, one lemma per norm: L2 [lintegral_slice_sq_le], H^j [ofReal_sobXSq_le with integral_unitCube_norm_iteratedFDeriv_sq_le], Fubini+dilation [lintegral_slab]); (3) eq:native-full-Cartan in the cellwise L^infty form (|R_h^raw(u_h)_{mu nu}(x) - e Riem(g_h)(z) e^-1| <= C h K^3 for every z in the cell of every node; the L2(Q) form follows with |Q|^{1/2}), native_cartan_riem at the full field. lem:native-plaquette.title: Regularity of the plaquette map
lem:native-plaquette.note: Proved in a real Banach algebra 𝔄 with ‖1‖ = 1 (NormOneClass; scoped hypothesis, as in the previous partial), for X, Y, a, b in 𝔄. Bundled statement exists_joint_analytic_extension: there is Φ : ℝ × 𝔄⁴ → 𝔄 (jointLogPlaquette) with (i) Φ analytic at every (0, X, Y, a, b), (ii) Φ(0; X,Y,a,b) = a - b + [X,Y], (iii) h² Φ(h) = log(e^{hX} e^{h(Y+ha)} e^{-h(X+hb)} e^{-hY}) for all h ≠ 0 with the series logarithm log(1+z) = z Σ (-1)^n z^n/(n+1), and (iv) for every order k and every compact set K of parameters there are h₀ > 0 and C with ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k Φ (h, q)‖ ≤ C for |h| ≤ h₀ and q ∈ K, i.e. all fixed-order derivatives in h and in the parameters are uniformly bounded on compact argument sets for small h (second sentence of the lemma). The 'analytic branch' is identified: exp(log(1+z)) = 1 + z for ‖z‖ < 1 (exp_logOneAdd, proved by differentiating t ↦ exp(-log(1+tz))(1+tz) with a Commute-based derivative of exp, no commutativity of 𝔄 needed), hence exp(h² Φ(h)) = P(h) whenever ‖P(h) - 1‖ < 1 (exp_sq_smul_logPlaquette). Method for (i)/(iv): exp u = 1 + u + u² E(u) with E entire (exp_eq_expRemainder), giving the explicit removable quotient P(h) - 1 = h² Q(h; X,Y,a,b) with Q a polynomial in h, X, Y, a, b and the E(h v_i) (product_sub_one_eq), equal to the dslope quotient of the previous partial for every h (quotient_eq_quotientPoly); Φ = Q · L(h² Q) is then jointly analytic on the open set ‖h² Q‖ < 1 ⊇ {0} × 𝔄⁴, and the bound (iv) follows by continuity of iteratedFDeriv on a compact tube [-h₀, h₀] × K (generalized tube lemma). Not restated separately: the one-variable h-derivatives are directional derivatives of the joint Fréchet derivatives, so they are covered by (iv).

lem:native-scaling.title: Differential-order scaling
lem:native-scaling.note: Proved. The four densities of eq:native-densities are defined concretely (NativeDensity.gravityDensity/ymDensity/higgsDensity/diracDensity, nativeDensity, localAction = h^4 sum) on the periodic grid from the link data of NativeScalingBlocksExact: v(e)=sqrt(-det g), g^{mu nu}=(e^T eta e)^{-1}, e_a^mu e^{b nu}=(e^{-1})^mu_a (e^{-1} eta)^nu_b, gamma^mu(e)=(e^{-1})^mu_a gamma^a, the Cartan plaquette logarithm R^h (series log of lem:native-plaquette, computed in the operator algebra of R^4 via the algebra map Mat -> Op), the gauge field strength F^h, the Higgs link K^h, the Dirac differences with spin link V=e^{h sigma(omega)} rho_S(U) and its explicit inverse V^{-1}=rho_S(U^{-1})e^{-h sigma(omega)} (certified by spinLink_mul_spinLinkInv), potential lambda_H(|H|^2-v_H^2)^2, Yukawa mass term. Main theorem nativeDensity_eq_scaled: for all h,K != 0 and every record, L_h(y)(x) = K^2 normB(hK, K^{-1}, Xi) + K normD(hK, K^{-1}, Xi) exactly, where Xi is the shifted first jet (ShiftedJetAction.stencil over the shifts 0,+-e_mu) of the record together with that of the normalised coframe connection omega~_rho = Omega(e, delta^+_rho e); the cosmological, potential and mass coefficients carry nu^2, nu^2, nu. Summed form localAction_eq_scaled, function identity localAction_eq_scaled_fun, and the Euler-row clause fderiv_localAction_eq_scaled (fderiv S_h = K^2 fderiv A~^B + K fderiv A~^D, given differentiability of the normalised actions). Regularity clause: contDiffAt_normB / contDiffAt_normD (C^infty in (rho,nu,jet) at every point with rho=0, any nu, det e != 0 at the base node) and exists_uniform_bound_normB / exists_uniform_bound_normD (for every order k and compact set of jets in the nondegenerate chart there are rho_0>0, C with all k-th Frechet derivatives bounded by C for |rho|<=rho_0, 0<=nu<=1). Renderings disclosed: (1) the normalised bosonic density is written as a function of the shifted first jets of the record and of omega~_rho (as in the paper's proof 'omega_h = K omega~_rho'), not of second differences of e; the Dirac density depends on the record's jet only; (2) representation data are abstract: rho_H, rho_S continuous algebra homomorphisms, sigma continuous linear, gamma^a arbitrary operators, invariant/Hermitian forms continuous bilinear, Yukawa map continuous linear in H; Higgs and spinor spaces real Banach spaces (Nontrivial), co-spinors are complex-valued functionals, complex structure otherwise unused; (3) plaquettes defined for mu<nu are extended antisymmetrically; (4) 'uniformly regular' rendered as C^infty with uniform derivative bounds on compacts (the growth hypothesis eq:growing-derivatives is not needed for the exact identity); (5) A a real Banach algebra with ||1||=1.

lem:nodal-source-transfer.title: From nodal Euler bounds to a physical source norm
lem:nodal-source-transfer.note: Proved. First clause (NodalSourceTransferExact.lean): ||f||_{L2(Q)} <= sqrt2 ||S_h f||_{0,h;Q'} + sqrt2 |Q'|^{1/2} h L for f with derivative bounded by L on Q', cells meeting Q contained in Q' (the buffer condition provided by Q compactly inside Q' and small h). The O(hK^3) clause is now DERIVED (NodalSourceJetChainExact.lean), not assumed: as in the paper's proof (differential degree <= 2), the Euler density is E_0 = F o j^2 y with j^2 y = (y, Dy, D^2 y) (jet2) and F C^1 on an open set containing a compact jet chart in which the jet of y stays on Q'; y is C^3 near Q' and satisfies eq:growing-derivatives literally on coordinate partial derivatives, ||D^n y(x)(e_{a1}, ..., e_{an})|| <= C K^n for 1 <= n <= 3 (only |alpha| <= 3 of the paper's |alpha| <= q, q >= 5 is used). Partial-derivative bounds give ||D^n y|| <= d^n C K^n (norm_le_card_pow_mul_of_basis), the chain rule gives ||D(j^2 y)|| <= d^3 C K^3 for K >= 1 (norm_jet2Deriv_le_growing), and compactness gives M >= 0 depending only on F and the chart with ||D E_0|| <= M d^3 C K^3 (euler_density_derivative_bound); hence ||E_0||_{L2(Q)} <= sqrt2 ||S_h E_0||_{0,h;Q'} + sqrt2 |Q'|^{1/2} (M d^3 C) h K^3 (eLpNorm_euler_density_le_nodalNorm). Disclosed: F is a general C^1 function of the 2-jet (the concrete Einstein-SM densities are instances); the final 'bounded invertible algebraic change to physical rows' (a fixed bounded linear map) is not formalised; sup norm on R^d. Checklist (l): the derivative bound is no longer a hypothesis; (h): F only C^1 near a compact chart.

lem:native-tail-transfer.title: Finite-order tail bounds
lem:native-tail-transfer.note: e37: ALL CLAUSES PROVED (Sigma = T^3, time periodic box; period-2pi rendering of the record reconstruction, n odd, h = 2pi/n). Setting: z_h = I_h^trig u_h = TrigInterp.recon n u (real trigonometric polynomial over the represented box |l|_inf <= (n-1)/2 with the DFT coefficients; it interpolates the record: recon_gpos), z_h^lo = reconLow n K u (frequencies |l|_inf <= K), tau_{h,j}(K) = sum over the deleted frequencies of (1+|l|_1/K)^j(|a_l|+|b_l|) (TrigInterp.tau; |u_hat| rendered as |a|+|b|). lem:half-ricci.title: Twisted half-Ricci contraction
lem:half-ricci.note: Proved as a pointwise algebraic identity: for a Clifford frame (c_a in any associative real algebra, ε_a = ±1, c_ac_b + c_bc_a = -2ε_aδ_ab, any finite index type) and any array R_abcd antisymmetric in both pairs with the first Bianchi identity, Σ_b ε_b c_b R^∇_ba = ½Σ_b ε_b (Σ_c ε_c R_cabc) c_b + Σ_b ε_b c_b ρ(F_ba), where R^∇ = ¼Σ ε_cε_d R_abcd c_c c_d + ρ(F) (twisted_half_ricci_contraction; half_ricci_contraction; with the contraction Σ_c ε_c R_cacb the sign of the Ricci term flips, half_ricci_contraction_opposite). Convention matching: the paper's Ric_ab = R^c_{acb} = Σ_c ε_c Riem_cacb, and the true spin curvature for this Clifford sign is -¼Σ Riem_abcd c^c c^d; instantiating R := -Riem gives eq:half-ricci verbatim for the geometric twisted curvature with the paper's Ricci convention (the displayed R^S formula of the manuscript must be read with R_abcd = -Riem_abcd, or carry -¼). The identification of R with the torsion-free spin-connection curvature and of ρ(F) with the gauge curvature is the lemma's setting, not part of the algebraic claim.

The uniformly spacelike slices and bounded lapse and shift give a positive wave energy': a nonzero shift is allowed, so option (a)): SlabWaveShiftEnergy.lean builds the normal-derivative-multiplier energy E_S = int sum_b ((d_t u - beta^k d_k u)^2 + a^{ij} d_i u d_j u + u^2), a = gamma + beta beta (= N^2 h^{-1}): pointwise identity d_t e - div J = G free of second derivatives (shift_alg), G <= K |first jets|^2, sqrt_energyS_le (L^1_t L^2_x source, Gronwall), sqrt_energyS_le_of_forcing, the H^k version hkS_energy / hkS_energy_of_forcing via the existing prolongation (SysHyp with an arbitrary gamma-coercivity constant + coercivity of a + |d_t beta| bound), energySK_ge, energySK_le_size, energySK_tendsto_zero. prop:homogeneous.title: A nonvacuum Einstein--Higgs comparison family

(iii) einstein_equations_of_constraint / einstein_equations_along_solution: with adot = a H, addot = a(H^2 + Hdot), Hdot = -(kappa/2) pi^2 and the constraint, all 16 components of G + Lambda g = kappa T^H hold on the flat FLRW jet (flrw_ricci_diag, flrw_scalar), T^H being eq:H-stress on the ansatz (rho = pi^2/2 + U, p = pi^2/2 - U). lem:generated-physical-identification.title: Physical identification of the symmetric extension
lem:generated-physical-identification.note: g15 (10 Oct 2026, IN PROGRESS): coupled (Dirac back-reaction) lift. SYMMETRISER FOUND (derivation G15_DERIVATION.md): the (Y, C, dC) system loses a derivative only because the normal prolongation defect P = (D'Y)_0 - R_0 (Clifford-curl / Lichnerowicz constraint of the auxiliary jets) is missing; with P adjoined, (Y, Ybar, P, Pbar, C) is symmetric hyperbolic with block-diagonal principal part and zero-order couplings. Proved so far (sorry-free): GenCpl.coupled_unique (generic coupled wave/first-order uniqueness), GenSFJ.kap_dirac_dirac (kappa(D'D'Y) order zero), GenDStress.symTD/CoupledDirac/quatCoupled (symmetric Dirac stress, back-reacting instance), GenCplEin.etr_eq/reduced_einstein_cpl (metric rows), GenCplX.x_row_cpl (spinor rows), GenCplCov.q_row (covariant rows), GenCplN.kap_DQ, GenCplP.P_dirac (Dirac equation of P). Remaining: bounds, C-equation source bound, Dirac stress Noether, dual blocks, assembly. EARLIER: g14 (10 Oct 2026): STAYS PROVED for theory data with decoupled spinors (GenPhysIdFinal.generated_physical_identification, _variational); disclosure (a) is NOT lifted, MANUSCRIPT FINDING. The obstruction is not the data model (SMData already lets Jcur and SH depend on (Psi, Psibar) and carries a Dirac-Yukawa stress form TD; e.g. SlabData.toSMData has the Dirac current, the Yukawa source and the symmetrised Dirac stress) but the PROPAGATION ARGUMENT. With back-reacting spinors the metric p-rows of the actual-jet system carry kappa trRev T^D(Psi, X) evaluated at the AUXILIARY tangential spinor jets X_a of the state (normal jet from the Dirac equation). For a solution W of the shift-transported system with constrained data all other sectors still propagate exactly as in g7 (metric g/q; gauge B via the reconstructed Bianchi identity; Higgs Q and Pi), the Dirac and dual Dirac equations of the head tuple z still follow from the psi-rows, and the Gauss constraint propagates once the current Noether identity includes the Dirac current (the E- and Pi-rows do not involve X). What remains are the X-defect Y_a = X_a(W) - nabla_{e_a}Psi(z) (and its dual) and the harmonic defect C, and the rows give exactly: (i) subtracting the p-rows of W and of the actual-jet state of z, E^tr(z) = kappa trRev(T^D(X(W)) - T^D(nabla Psi)) - G(C, dC)/(2N), so the X-rows give c^b nabla_b Y_a = (order 0 in Y) + c^b nabla_(a C_b) Psi: the X-defect is sourced by FIRST derivatives of C; (ii) the contracted Bianchi identity of z gives Box C + Ric C = -2 kappa div Delta T^D(Y) with Delta T^D_AB = sym <Psibar, c_A Y_B> + (dual) (its trace part vanishes since c^A Y_A = 0), and modulo the Y-rows div Delta T^D_B is a nonzero multiple of <Psibar, c_B K(Y)> plus lower order, with the Clifford curl K(Y) = Sum_{i != j} c_i c_j d_j Y_i, which the Y-rows (they control only the Dirac combinations c^b nabla_b Y_a) do not determine. The defect system is therefore coupled at first order in BOTH directions (C <- dY, Y <- dC; both blocks have the light cone as characteristic set, the composite loses one derivative), no L^2 or H^k energy closes, and the decoupled argument (spinor-free tuple physical first, then X by state uniqueness) has no analogue. Lifting needs either a constraint-propagating symmetric formulation of the prolonged Einstein-Dirac system (constraint additions coupling the X-curl to the metric rows symmetrically) or the analytic-core/physical-Cauchy clause of ass:constrained-initial-solver (persistence of analyticity plus Holmgren-type uniqueness for the linear defect system; not formalised). Suggested manuscript amendment: as written, the propagation route of lem:generated-physical-identification covers T^D = 0 only; for back-reacting spinors the lemma rests on the physical-Cauchy clause of ass:constrained-initial-solver. DATA CLASS: the constrained class is the actual-jet class GenPhysIdClosed.ConstrainedData (smooth data); the bridge from prop:generated-initial is NOT done (see cor:generated-nonempty: abstract conformal interface, finite-regularity conformal factor vs smooth data class, no Cauchy-data completion lemma). Non-vacuity with NONZERO, CHARGED spinors: quatSM (spinor space H x H = R^8 with the real Cl_{1,3} module c_0 = swap, c_i = diag(q_i, -q_i), gauge U(1) subset GL(1) acting by right multiplication by i, scalar Yukawa coupling, transposed co-spinor block), quatVariationalDirac and the example (CurrentNoether quatSM, Nontrivial (H x H), mu_S(Psibar, c_0 Psi) != 0). So the Gauss-sector input of the coupled propagation is available; NOT done: the stress Noether identity with the symmetric Dirac stress (needs the spinor Ricci identity and half-Ricci contraction at field level, with first derivatives of the Dirac residuals in the off-shell identity), and, as explained above, the X-defect/harmonic propagation is obstructed. prop:native-reader.title: Exact native-energy to physical-tail certificate
prop:native-reader.note: Finite-dimensional linear algebra, fully proved; the revised statement matches the Lean even more closely than the old one. Source space H = finite-dimensional real inner-product space, native energy Q symmetric with <xi,Q xi> >= 0, coefficient map T : H -> (modes -> F) linear, positive weights w, tail tau_w(v) = sum_l w_l ||v_l|| (the l^1(w) norm). eq:source-reader-linear / eq:source-reader-kernel: exists_readerConstant_iff_kernel states that a finite c with ||T xi||_{l^1(w)} <= c <xi,Q xi>^{1/2} for ALL xi in H (IsReaderConstant, quantified over the entire source space, so not inferred from a finite list of legal states) exists iff T(ker Q) = 0 (KernelCondition). eq:source-reader-constant: readerConstant := ||T Q^{dagger/2}||_{2->l^1(w)} = sup_{||y||<=1} tau_w(T Q^{dagger/2} y), with Q^{dagger/2} = SpectralDiag.pinvSqrt built from Mathlib's finite spectral theorem (lambda_i^{-1/2} on the nonzero spectrum, 0 on the kernel); symmetric, positive, and its square satisfies the Penrose identities Q Q^dagger Q = Q and Q^dagger Q Q^dagger = Q^dagger (Q_pinvSq_Q, pinvSq_Q_pinvSq), so it is the positive square root of the Moore-Penrose inverse; readerConstant_isLeast: under the kernel condition this constant is admissible and is the least nonnegative admissible constant. eq:source-reader-tail ("in particular"): affine_reader_tail derives tau_w(u^soft + T xi) <= tau_w(u^soft) + c <xi,Q xi>^{1/2} for the affine reader u = u^soft + R xi by the triangle inequality. Disclosed: T is any linear coefficient map (its identification with the |l|_inf > K weighted Fourier coefficients of R_h xi is carried abstractly); optimality is stated among nonnegative constants.
